NKJV.1: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok.
NKJV.2: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah had done (although he did not enter the temple of the LORD). But still the people acted corruptly.
NKJV.3: He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and he built extensively on the wall of Ophel.
NKJV.4: Moreover he built cities in the mountains of Judah, and in the forests he built fortresses and towers.
NKJV.5: He also fought with the king of the Ammonites and defeated them. And the people of Ammon gave him in that year one hundred talents of silver, ten thousand kors of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. The people of Ammon paid this to him in the second and third years also.
NKJV.6: So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the LORD his God.
NKJV.7: Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars and his ways, indeed they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
NKJV.8: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
NKJV.9: So Jotham rested with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David. Then Ahaz his son reigned in his place.

NASB.1: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok.
NASB.2: He did right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah had done; however he did not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people continued acting corruptly.
NASB.3: He built the upper gate of the house of the LORD, and he built extensively the wall of Ophel.
NASB.4: Moreover, he built cities in the hill country of Judah, and he built fortresses and towers on the wooded [hills].
NASB.5: He fought also with the king of the Ammonites and prevailed over them so that the Ammonites gave him during that year one hundred talents of silver, ten thousand kors of wheat and ten thousand of barley. The Ammonites also paid him this [amount] in the second and in the third year.
NASB.6: So Jotham became mighty because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God.
NASB.7: Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, even all his wars and his acts, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
NASB.8: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
NASB.9: And Jotham slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Ahaz his son became king in his place.

NLT.1: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years. His mother was Jerusha, the daughter of Zadok.
NLT.2: Jotham did what was pleasing in the LORD’s sight. He did everything his father, Uzziah, had done, except that Jotham did not sin by entering the Temple of the LORD. But the people continued in their corrupt ways.
NLT.3: Jotham rebuilt the upper gate of the Temple of the LORD. He also did extensive rebuilding on the wall at the hill of Ophel.
NLT.4: He built towns in the hill country of Judah and constructed fortresses and towers in the wooded areas.
NLT.5: Jotham went to war against the Ammonites and conquered them. Over the next three years he received from them an annual tribute of 7,500 pounds of silver, 50,000 bushels of wheat, and 50,000 bushels of barley.
NLT.6: King Jotham became powerful because he was careful to live in obedience to the LORD his God.
NLT.7: The rest of the events of Jotham’s reign, including all his wars and other activities, are recorded in The Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
NLT.8: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years.
NLT.9: When Jotham died, he was buried in the City of David. And his son Ahaz became the next king.

CSB17.1: Jotham was twenty-five years old <sup>ⓔ</sup> when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. <sup>ⓕ</sup> His mother’s name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
CSB17.2: He did what was right in the LORD’s sight just as his father Uzziah had done. In addition, he didn’t enter the LORD’s sanctuary, <sup>ⓖ</sup> but the people still behaved corruptly.
CSB17.3: Jotham built the Upper Gate of the LORD’s temple, and he built extensively on the wall of Ophel. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.4: He also built cities in the hill country of Judah and fortresses and towers in the forests. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.5: He waged war against the king of the Ammonites. He overpowered the Ammonites, and that year they gave him 7,500 pounds <sup>[1]</sup> of silver, 50,000 bushels <sup>[2]</sup> of wheat, and 50,000 bushels of barley. They paid him the same in the second and third years.
CSB17.6: So Jotham strengthened his position because he did not waver in obeying <sup>[3]</sup> the LORD his God. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.7: As for the rest of the events <sup>ⓚ</sup> of Jotham’s reign, along with all his wars and his ways, note that they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
CSB17.8: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
CSB17.9: Jotham rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of David. His son Ahaz became king in his place.

NIV.1:
Jotham King of Judah
Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years. His mother’s name was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
NIV.2: He did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, just as his father Uzziah had done, but unlike him he did not enter the temple of the Lord. The people, however, continued their corrupt practices.
NIV.3: Jotham rebuilt the Upper Gate of the temple of the Lord and did extensive work on the wall at the hill of Ophel.
NIV.4: He built towns in the Judean hills and forts and towers in the wooded areas.
NIV.5: Jotham made war on the king of the Ammonites and conquered them. That year the Ammonites paid him a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat and ten thousand cors of barley. The Ammonites brought him the same amount also in the second and third years.
NIV.6: Jotham grew powerful because he walked steadfastly before the Lord his God.
NIV.7: The other events in Jotham’s reign, including all his wars and the other things he did, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
NIV.8: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years.
NIV.9: Jotham rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And Ahaz his son succeeded him as king.

MSG.1: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king; he reigned sixteen years at Jerusalem. His mother was Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.
MSG.2: In God's eyes he lived a good life, following the path marked out by his father Uzziah. Unlike his father, though, he didn't desecrate The Temple of God. But the people pushed right on in their lives of corruption.
MSG.3: Jotham constructed the Upper Gate of The Temple of God, considerably extended the Wall of the Ophel,
MSG.4: and built cities in the high country of Judah and forts and towers down in the forests.
MSG.5: He fought and beat the king of the Ammonites—that year the Ammonites turned over three and a quarter tons of silver and about sixty-five bushels of wheat, and another sixty-five bushels of barley. They repeated this for the next two years.
MSG.6: Jotham's strength was rooted in his steady and determined life of obedience to God.
MSG.7: The rest of the history of Jotham, including his wars and achievements, are all written in the Royal Annals of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
MSG.8: He was twenty-five years old when he became king; he reigned for sixteen years at Jerusalem.
MSG.9: Jotham died and was buried in the City of David. His son Ahaz became the next king.

NET.1: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.
NET.2: He did what the LORD approved, just as his father Uzziah had done. (He did not, however, have the audacity to enter the temple.) Yet the people were still sinning.
NET.3: He built the Upper Gate to the LORD’s temple and did a lot of work on the wall in the area known as Ophel.
NET.4: He built cities in the hill country of Judah and fortresses and towers in the forests.
NET.5: He launched a military campaign against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them. That year the Ammonites paid him 100 talents of silver, 10,000 kors of wheat, and 10,000 kors of barley. The Ammonites also paid this same amount of annual tribute the next two years.
NET.6: Jotham grew powerful because he was determined to please the LORD his God.
NET.7: The rest of the events of Jotham’s reign, including all his military campaigns and his accomplishments, are recorded in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.
NET.8: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem.
NET.9: Jotham passed away and was buried in the City of David. His son Ahaz replaced him as king.
